title: Behind the Front Page: Bigfoot spotted in local woods
excerpt: I’m getting too old for this stuff.
content:
I’m getting too old for this stuff.

No, I’m not talking about holding my breath on every pitch of the World Series, although that would be true as well. As of this writing on Tuesday morning the Crew is up 3-0. For the sake of my ticker and many more in Wisconsin, let’s hope by the time you read this it’s all over. More on that next week, I’m sure.

What I’m talking about is how I’ve been spending my Saturday nights over the last three weekends, and it will be Friday and Saturday night this coming weekend.

As I alluded to in this column a few weeks ago, I’ve been helping out at the Haunted Cart Rides at Hickory Hills Country Club near Chilton—at least on the nights I wasn’t covering high school football. I also gave you a clue that what I was doing had something to do with the Patterson-Gimlin film. I’m guessing some of you knew what that meant, and maybe others Googled it.

The Patterson-Gimlin film is the famous 1967 short film clip which supposedly showed a Bigfoot walking through the woods. Many people claim there is evidence that the film was a hoax. I’m not here today to debate or discuss that, although I will say that even if that film was a hoax it doesn’t mean all sightings are hoaxes. I’m on the side of the many park rangers, police officers, soldiers, clergy members and others (but not the hoaxers) who say they have seen them.

I’ve never done anything like this before and I wasn’t sure what to expect, and I did have some trepidation going into it—mostly how my body would hold up. I’m guessing that at 65 years old, I might be the oldest “spook” in those woods. I have surprised myself at how much Bigfoot shuffling I’ve done in chasing after carts, or leaping out from behind a tree, or emulating Bigfoot activity by tugging on a small tree.

What hasn’t surprised me is how beat I am after three to four hours of running around in the woods. I haven’t felt too terribly bad the day after, except for the day I got the worst leg cramp in my life. I was sure the muscle was about to emulate the famous scene from “Alien” and burst out of my thigh. Now that would have been scary!

One thing which has surprised me is how ignorant many cart riders are about my character and that of my fellow Bigfoot, Matt. By the way, I wonder if real Bigfoot have names for each other? Also, please note that mankind has yet to settle on the proper plural form of Bigfoot. Is it just Bigfoot (like “sheep” or “deer”), or is it Bigfoots, or is it Bigfeet? That remains almost as big a mystery as whether or not they really exist.

Anyway, people keep saying some form of, “Look, it’s a gorilla!” So far I’ve stayed in character and haven’t spoken, but I’m getting real close to yelling, “I’m not a damn gorilla, I’m Bigfoot!” What are we teaching our kids in school these days? Do I have to volunteer to teach a Sasquatch 101 class?

I’m also not surprised at the occasional smart-aleck comments, usually from young men. Look, I fill out the costume nicely. I’ve heard people say, “That’s a big dude!” But no, I’m not pregnant, as one guy said. Do you see breasts on me? And, yes, female Bigfoot with breasts have been spotted many times. Skinny Bigfoot also have been spotted but it is believed they may be sickly. I’m a healthy Bigfoot, thank you very much!

I do live for the jump scares and the screamers. Screaming teenage girls and petrified middle age women are hilarious, at least to me. It also is very satisfying to “get” the big, brave men who didn’t see me coming. And just so you know, the cart rides do have a system for warning us to tone it down for little ones who might scare easily.

Playing Bigfoot has been a blast. I’ll see where I’m at physically next year and whether or not I reprise the role—that is, if watching the Brewers in the World Series doesn’t kill me first.
